Protective factors include ongoing employment and some insight into their stress.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Work-related stress
- Patient Goal(s): Symptom relief; coping with work stress; improve well-being
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce stress levels; monitor for escalation of symptoms; support coping mechanisms
- Actions (Patient):
  - Utilize clinician-provided information on self-care for dermatitis
  - Monitor symptoms and follow-up if stress or skin symptoms persist
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provided educational leaflet about dermatitis
  - Recommended emollients, topical steroid, and OTC antihistamines for skin symptoms
  - Advised follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen
  - Linked stress as a possible contributing factor; encouraged self-monitoring

Secondary Problem (if applicable): Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Dermatitis, self-care measures, stress as a potential factor, use of topical therapies and antihistamines
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistence or worsening of skin symptoms; sustained high stress or psychosocial decline
- Coping Strategies: Self-care for dermatitis; monitor/manage work-related stress; seek medical review if persistent
